title: INKOPATION - math rock rhythm game.  I'm having a blast making games, I think they're extremely fun
author: ConcernedParsnip
selftext:
I'm having fun but I'm not sure if anyone else wants to play them.  My first post blew up on playmygame of the first game I made, The Inkline, but tried to post it again and it was largely ignored.  Still there but have also made another one... You need to keep pressing in time with changing time signatures.  Game evolves to have multiple tracks each with different time signatures at the same time in moderate, hard or extreme (4 of them) mode.

AI has helped prototype this... clearly...  Ultimately it would be lovely to redo all of this by hand, have music I have made but I'm only one person with so much time..> I just love the fact we can put ideas to reality now and create something really quite cool

  
[https://inklinestudios.itch.io/inkopation](https://inklinestudios.itch.io/inkopation)

comments.author: StaticAnchor
comments.body:
I think you might really have something here.

I’m a sucker for rhythm games on mobile and see the potential for a resurgence in this space.

I feel the potential in it, I don’t think you are imagining it. A couple of thoughts.

The UI at the start needs refinement, a lot of people could get turned off right there. I’d maybe have gameplay in the background and you seeing the settings change as you select what level you want to play. A sample of the song, etc.

On the setting, it feels like there’s different aesthetics that make it all not feel part of the same world. I thought the strongest level was either the first or second. Something about finding the rhythm to bring color to the world works.

I’d make the colors mean something. Maybe a streak and the colors shift at different points. Whatever it is, make it intentional.

You need to give the players a buffer after they die. In rhythm games you need a chance to get back into flow, there were moments where I respawned and almost instantly died. Respawn the player in areas that are safer, and maybe cap the lives at 3.

What’s working is the feel. It just generally feels fun, which I think is one of the hardest things to find making a game. I liked the moment of the split paths. Maybe don’t call out a hard or easy path, but maybe have one that feels more enticing to go into, like coins or something. It felt sort of Sonic-esque, lots of possibilities in choosing a different path. Maybe it’s a different instrument. Let the player feel the risk vs reward without explicitly saying it too. liked the coin moment, to do a move “off beat” that could kill you is a rewarding moment.

Another thing that I think would work here are songs that start slow and build up to be faster. It would be cool if the song was dynamic, where the more on beat you are the faster the game gets. The best parts of the game were the higher tempo parts, and being brought out of that hurt, so maybe the world slows down if you die.

Excited to see where this goes, good luck!

replies.author: ConcernedParsnip
replies.body:
Amazing thank you for such a great and helpful reply.  Yes to all of the above.  Some of the spawn points are just ridiculous, in the split mode (moderate and above) it automatically does the first beat for you after a respawn and that helps get back into it.

I’m mindful not to make it toooo hard.  I love challenging games but have been messing about with poki and people just up and leave when it’s difficult… although… maybe it’s just not for that audience.  

Really helpful feedback, thank you

replies.author: StaticAnchor
replies.body:
Agreed on not too hard, no one wants to play Through The Fire and Flames on their first play through lol.

Just a moment of pace picking up where the second half of the level is 10BPM higher I think would be enough of a…oh wow moment. Too slow and people might go, oh that’s neat and move on.

Have fun!
